International patient revenue, Egypt Healthcare Authority, 2025

key_takeaways: Out-of-pocket payments covered 57 percent of current health spending in 2023, sustaining private demand among those who can pay.{{health_system.private_system:5}}
Second-phase Universal Health Insurance is planned to reach about 13 million people, with investment of more than EGP 115 billion.{{health_system.outlook:1}}{{health_system.outlook:2}}
Only 38 percent of doctors licensed in Egypt work in the country, according to the Egyptian Medical Syndicate.{{health_system.workforce:4}}
Egypt is seeking a foreign operator for a planned Cairo medical city with 4,000 beds.{{health_system.outlook:4}}{{recent_developments.0:1}}
health_system: University hospitals grew from 88 in 2013 to 147 in 2026.{{health_system.public_system:3}}

Phase one of Universal Health Insurance is complete in six governorates; Minya starts phase two with a one-year trial.{{health_system.public_system:2}}{{health_system.public_system:1}}{{health_system.public_system:5}}
Government health spending was 1.6 percent of GDP in 2023, below the Constitution's commitment of at least 3 percent.{{health_system.financing:4}}{{health_system.financing:6}}
market: Cleopatra Hospitals Group had about 1,000 operating beds at the end of 2025 across 17 facilities.{{health_system.private_system:1}}

Saudi German Hospital Cairo joined the Mayo Clinic Care Network in 2019; the group expanded the relationship in October 2025.{{health_system.private_system:2}}{{health_system.private_system:7}}{{health_system.private_system:8}}
Private providers make up 35 percent of contracted providers under Universal Health Insurance.{{health_system.public_system:2}}
risks: The IMF expects inflation to rise to about 16.7 percent in the second half of 2026.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:2}}
Bed density fell from 1.4 per 1,000 in 2011 to 1.06 in 2021 as the population grew faster than capacity.{{health_system.workforce:3}}
Universal Health Insurance phase two depends on financing, and the law is being amended so the authority stays solvent.{{health_system.outlook:3}}

recent.text: The Healthcare Authority reported treating about 35,000 patients from 124 countries in 2025, with revenue of about $8 million.{{recent_developments.2:1}}
The health minister said Minya, home to about seven million people, will lead phase two on a one-year trial.{{recent_developments.3:1}}
The IMF Executive Board completed the seventh Extended Fund Facility review, releasing about $1.77 billion.{{recent_developments.4:1}}{{recent_developments.4:2}}

country_background: Egypt, with about 108.6 million people at the start of 2026, is a republic with a directly elected president and a bicameral parliament, and its capital is Cairo.{{country_overview.demographics:1}}{{country_overview.demographics:5}} President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was sworn in for a third six-year term in April 2024, and Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly leads the cabinet.{{country_overview.government:2}}{{country_overview.government:3}} Egypt is one of the largest Arab economies, with GDP of about $2.39 trillion on a purchasing power parity basis in 2025.{{country_overview.economy:5}} Consumer price inflation was 14.1 percent in 2025 after 28.3 percent in 2024.{{country_overview.economy:4}} The total fertility rate fell to 2.41 in 2024, and only about 43 percent of people live in urban areas.{{country_overview.demographics:9}}{{country_overview.demographics:11}} Deputy Health Minister Amr Kandil said in September 2025 that noncommunicable diseases account for about 80 percent of deaths.{{country_overview.disease_prevalence:1}} The key risk is inflation: the IMF expects it to rise to about 16.7 percent in the second half of 2026, delaying its return to the central bank's target range by about a year.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:2}}
